title: cvpw render/report.json
description: The record of one render: what was drawn, by what, how fast, and which encoder was actually selected. Derived and never an input to a stage (docs/SPEC.md A6). See docs/CONTRACTS.md §10.

verified.description: What ffprobe reports the FILE contains, as opposed to `frames`, which is what the frame sink wrote. The two disagreeing is the failure `render.frameCount` exists to catch, so both are recorded rather than one being trusted.

output.description: Project-relative path of the encoded file.

codec.description: The codec actually used, after probing. Never the requested one.

codecRequested.description: What was asked for, which may differ when probing found the hardware encoder unusable.

codecProbe.description: The evidence: the probe's exit code or message. `h264_nvenc` being listed by ffmpeg is not evidence.

renderer.description: The WebGL renderer string the browser reported for this render.

software.description: True when the render ran under a software rasteriser. Its float paths differ, so the file is a different artefact and the report must say so.

resolvedTimes.description: Shot id to resolved seconds. Written so a time expression's effect can be audited after the fact.

resolvedExpressions.description: Shot id to the time expression it came from. With resolvedTimes, this makes a re-cut's effect reviewable.

frameHashes.description: Frame index to content hash at the sampled times. The determinism witness (docs/SPEC.md D7).

registry.description: What was registered when this render ran, so a file can be traced to the code set that produced it.

errors.description: A non-empty list means the output file was deleted. A truncated render must never masquerade as a finished one.
